text:
marie: Quick heads-up — Q3 hosted API GPU runway. model-level traffic ramps in July; our run-rate sim shows a ~18% shortfall if we don't add capacity by mid‑June. Thinking about staggered PO windows + short-term rentals to smooth delivery and avoid customs bottlenecks.
jon: Do you have the raw numbers for the sim? need to show finance before we open RFQs.
marie: putting numbers here — rough daily GPU-hour need (A100-80GB equiv):
```
month,avg_rps,avg_seq_len,est_tokens_per_day,gpu_hours_needed_per_day
May,1200,512,1.7e9,420
Jun,1500,520,2.1e9,520
Jul,2100,560,2.9e9,720
Aug,1900,540,2.6e9,640
```
Also used 1.9M tokens per GPU-hour baseline. headroom target = 20%.
siva: note APAC shipments: import windows gone from 3w to 6-8w depending on vendor. if we rely on on-prem delivery for apac, that could push usable capacity into late july.
anya: +1 on staggered approach. we should also reserve a warm pool (~100 GPUs) in us-west for low-latency tails and to reduce queue spikes. warm pool can be preemptible where acceptable.
ricardo: cost quick compare (list price equiv /hour): reserved amortized = $1.60/hr, short-term rental = $3.40/hr, preemptible = $0.85/hr but with 20% preemption risk. If we do 50/30/20 split (buy/rent/preemptible) estimated blended = $1.95/hr.
capacity-bot: simulation complete — projected runway breach date = 2026-07-18, fallback margin if we accept 15% preemptible = 9%. recommend PO timing: 40% immediate, 40% delivery in 6 weeks, 20% rentals for overflow. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
marie: actionable ask — @jon can you draft an RFQ and ping our procurement vendors? @siva can you validate APAC lead times with vendor ops? I'll update the spreadsheet and run the final sim after vendor ETAs.
jon: on it, will share draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
marie: thanks — planning sync tomorrow 10am to lock numbers. agenda: final sim, RFQ buyers list, warm-pool placement, finance signoff.
